claims.text: Resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation in high-entropy-alloy multilayer protective coatings is governed by interactions between grain boundaries, dislocation networks, and alloy composition.
Interactions among grain boundaries, dislocation networks, and alloy composition hinder dislocation glide.
Interactions among grain boundaries, dislocation networks, and alloy composition hinder dislocation climb.
Hindering dislocation glide and climb reduces creep rates.
High-entropy-alloy multilayer protective coatings are expected to have reduced creep rates relative to monolithic high-entropy alloys or conventional coatings.
High-entropy-alloy multilayer protective coatings are expected to have improved resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation relative to monolithic high-entropy alloys or conventional coatings.
The proposed mechanism applies to as-deposited or annealed high-entropy-alloy multilayer protective coatings.
The proposed applicability range is 100–500 MPa.
Varying alloy composition and processing conditions during in-situ HRTEM creep testing can reveal whether grain-boundary and dislocation-network interactions govern creep resistance.
